correctness.rationale: Each section vertex almost surely corresponds to one crossed polytope edge. Haar probability of a sign-disagreement for two endpoint vectors is exactly their central angle divided by pi. Summing the m vertical and 2m horizontal edge contributions proves (1) and the O(h^-3) expansions. For centered cyclic K the exact derivative bracket B(t)=m-2 sum_i s_i t/sqrt(t^2+c_i^2) decreases strictly because all s_i,c_i>0, with B(0)=m and B(infinity)=m-P(K)/R. This proves the full iff unique finite maximum. Concavity on the constrained angular gap polytope gives strict P>4R, while Jensen gives P<=2mR sin(pi/m); explicit contrasting five-gon gaps and continuity prove the pentagon phase boundary, and the regular pentagon stationary equation gives the stated exact golden-ratio height. The checker script passes 135 comparisons including 770000 independently sampled random normals. Numerical tests are supplementary, not a proof.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus searches for cyclic prisms, mean section vertices, pentagonal height optimization, and angular edge-crossing equivalents were compared to the available descriptions of previously documented findings and to the material read in primary full texts. The all-cyclic strict perimeter threshold, five-gon regime bifurcation and pentagon golden optimum are not implied by the inspected deterministic slice-optimization theorem, the cube-only hexagon probability, the triangular-prism full distribution, or prism width-moment results. A source restricted to numerical distributions of section angles is bibliographically unresolved because its full text was inaccessible; this does not, on present evidence, create a decisive competing covering statement. Priority is not guaranteed.

value.rationale: The natural geometric-probability optimization of mean central-section vertex count is solved for the full family of centered cyclic bases: a single classical planar quantity P/R controls the existence, uniqueness and nonattainment of optimal prism height. In particular five-sided polygons exhibit a genuine perimeter-driven phase transition with examples in both regimes and an exact golden-ratio optimum for the regular shape. This is not just a small numerical gain or rephrasing of the previously known triangular prism and box cases; it provides a complete dimension-uniform side-count classification and a transferable edge-angle identity.
